mekayis.metin:
(أَوَقَ) الْهَمْزَةُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلَانِ: الْأَوَّلُ الثِّقَلُ، وَالثَّانِي مَكَانٌ مُنْهَبِطٌ. فَأَمَّا الْأَوَّلُ فَالْأَوْقُ الثِّقَلُ. قَالَ ابْنُ الْأَعْرَابِيِّ: يُقَالُ: آقَ عَلَيْهِمْ، أَيْ: ثَقُلَ. قَالَ:
سَوَائِحُ آقَ عَلَيْهِنَّ الْقَدَرْ ... يَهْوِينَ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ مَا لَاقَى الْأُخَرْ
يَقُولُ: أَثْقَلَهُنَّ مَا أَنْزَلَ بِالْأَوَّلِ الْقَدَرُ، فَهُنَّ يَخَفْنَ مِثْلَهُ. قَالَ يَعْقُوبُ: يُقَالُ: أَوَّقْتُ الْإِنْسَانَ: إِذَا حَمَّلْتُهُ مَا لَا يُطِيقُهُ. وَأَمَّا التَّأْوِيقُ فِي الطَّعَامِ فَهُوَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَيْضًا، لِأَنَّ عَلَى النَّفْسِ مِنْهُ ثِقَلًا، وَذَلِكَ تَأْخِيرُهُ وَتَقْلِيلُهُ. قَالَ:
لَقَدْ كَانَ حُتْرُوشُ بْنُ عَزَّةَ رَاضِيًا ... سِوَى عَيْشِهِ هَذَا بِعَيْشٍ مُؤَوَّقِ
وَقَالَ الرَّاجِزُ:
عَزَّ عَلَى عَمِّكِ أَنْ تُؤَوَّقي ... أَوْ أَنْ تَبِيِتي لَيْلَةً لَمْ تُغْبَقِي
أَوْ أَنْ تُرَيْ كَأْبَاءَ لَمْ تَبْرَنْشِقِي
وَأَمَّا الثَّانِي فَالْأُوقَةُ، وَهِيَ هَبْطَةٌ يَجْتَمِعُ فِيهَا الْمَاءُ، وَالْجَمْعُ الْأُوَقُ قَالَ رُؤْبَةُ:
وَانْغَمَسَ الرَّامِي لَهَا بَيْنَ الْأُوَقْ
وَيُقَالُ: الْأُوقَةُ الْقَلِيبُ.

anlam: awqiyyah (ounce), a unit of weight in Egypt: 37 grams (one twelfth ratl)
a unit of weight in Aleppo: 320 grams
a unit of weight in Beirut: 213.39 grams
a unit of weight in Jerusalem: 240 grams
a unit of weight in Morocco: approximately 62.5 grams
a unit of weight in Malta: approximately 26.46 grams
ouguiya (currency of Mauritania) (only in this form, not وُقِيَّة (wuqiyya))
ounce (just the same as the English or even to translate it)

vikisozluk.baslik: أَيْقُونِيّ • (ʔayqūniyy) (feminine أَيْقُونِيَّة (ʔayqūniyya), masculine plural أَيْقُونِيُّون (ʔayqūniyyūn), feminine plural أَيْقُونِيَّات (ʔayqūniyyāt))

vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: Probably through Classical Syriac ܐܘܢܩܝܐ (ʾūnqīyā) from Ancient Greek οὐγγία (oungía), οὐγκία (ounkía), from Latin uncia (“ounce, twelfth part”), from ūnus (“one”). Cognate with English ounce.
Ultimately from Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn). Sense 2 is a semantic loan from English icon.

Etymology tree
Arabic أَيْقُونَة (ʔayqūna)
Proto-Afroasiatic
Proto-Semitic
Arabic ـِيّ (-iyy)
Arabic أيقوني
From أَيْقُونَة (ʔayqūna, “icon”) + ـِيّ (-iyy). Calque of English iconic.

I, ‘to draw an evil ( ʕalà upon s.o.) | attirer sur qn qq malheur ( h h )’, D-stem † ʔawwaqa (II) ‘to burden s.o. | charger qn d’un fardeau, lui faire porter ou lui imposer une tâche rude et pénible ( h h ); tourmenter’ ▪ † ʔWQ_4 ‘se trouver sur une hauteur et dominer ( ʕalà ce qui est en bas); pendre d’en haut et surplomber’: † ʔāqa ▪ † ʔWQ_5 ‘empêcher’ : ʔawwaqa (II); cf. also taʔawwaqa (V) in the sense of ↗ taʕawwaqa ▪ ʔWQ_1: ~ ʔuqqaẗ (s.r. ↗√ʔQː (ʔQQ)), from Grk ὄγκος ( ógkos ) ‘mass, weight’ ▪ ʔWQ_2: ~ wuqiyyaẗ ~ EgAr wiq͗iyyaẗ ~ LevAr wuq͗iyyeẗ (s.r. ↗√WQY) : DRS 7 (1997) [#WNQ]: cascade d’emprunts: Gz waqet , ʕənqʷəya wuqiyyaẗ , ʔūqiyyaẗ (EgAr wiq͗iyyaẗ , HispAr waqí(y)a ) ʔunqā , ʔunqᵊyā , Syr ʔunqiyā , nᵊqūyā ) ougkía ) uncia . «Il s’agit d’un terme de mesure de poids, mesure qui, en Aram comme en Ar, est différente selon les sources et sans doute selon les lieux auxquels elle se réfère. Souvent, comme en Syr ou en Ar, le mot est utilisé pour signifier «un rien, un peu». ▪ † ʔWQ_3: denom. from [v1] ʔūqaẗ or an independent root? – The value ‘sorrow, misfortune’ is certainly figurative use, from ‘burden, weight’. ▪ † ʔWQ_4: The phon. identity of this ʔāqa with that of [v3] seems to point to a relation between both, but what could be the semantic link? ▪ † ʔWQ_5 : Although ʔawwaqa in the sense of ‘to hinder’ could be thought of as depending on † [v3] † ʔāqa (I) ‘to draw an evil upon s.o.’ (with the D-stem † ʔawwaqa ‘to burden s.o’), BK1860 considers this ʔawwaqa (II) to be a var. of ʕawwaqa (↗ʕWQ), as also the corresponding t -stem taʔawwaqa as a var. of taʕawwaqa (dto.). – ▪ ʔWQ_1 : ↗ ʔuqqaẗ ▪ ʔWQ_2 : DRS 7 (1997) [#WNQ]: TalmAram ʔunqā , ʔunqᵊyā , Syr ʔunqiyā , nᵊqūyā , Ar wuqiyyaẗ , ʔūqiyyaẗ , EgAr wiq͗iyyaẗ , HispAr waqí(y)a , Gz waqet , ʕənqʷəya , Te Tña Amh wəqet ‘once’. – Cf., however, below, section DISC. ▪ … ▪ ʔWQ_1–2: DRS seems to confuse [v1] and [v2] when the authors write : «originairement le ʔūqiyyaẗ contenait 40 dirhems (drachmes); en pharmacopée, le oukia compte douze drachmes. Aujourd’hui, l’ okke équivaut à deux livres et demie». Although there is considerable local and regional variation as to the actual weight of each of the two units, the ʔūqiyyaẗ ‘ounce’ is definitively much lighter (only parts of a ↗ raṭl ) than the ʔuqqaẗ (twice as heavy, or more, than a raṭl ). ▪ Accordingly, the cognates given in DRS may have to be separated: TalmAram ʔunqā , Gz waqet , Te Tña Amh wəqet may in fact be cognates of [v1] ʔuqqaẗ , while the items showing ‑y‑ (TalmAram ʔunqᵊyā , Syr ʔunqiyā , nᵊqūyā , Gz ʕənqʷəya ) may belong to [v2] Ar wuqiyyaẗ , ʔūqiyyaẗ , EgAr wiq͗iyyaẗ , HispAr waqí(y)a . ▪ … – – Sources ; meta ; gram ; engl ; conc ; hist ; cogn ; disc ; west ; deriv ;
